title: Central Asia’s Leaders Gather in Turkmenistan for 8th Consultative Meeting
author: Catherine Putz
text:
Credit: Facebook / Shavkat Mirziyoyev
On October 8, Turkmenistan hosted a flurry of region meetings in Avaza, including the 8th Consultative Meeting of the Heads of State of Central Asia and Azerbaijan, and the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) Council of Heads of State, as well as related foreign minister-level meetings. According to Turkmen state media, Turkmen President Serdar Berdimuhamedov laid out “five key objectives,” which included “building the potential of the six-party format,” ensuring lasting peace and stability in the region, joint efforts “to transform Central Asia and Azerbaijan into key transport, logistics, energy, and industrial hubs on the continent in the East-West and North-South directions,” creating the conditions for “accelerated technological growth and the active implementation of artificial intelligence,” and finally, expanding “cultural, humanitarian, educational, and civilizational ties.”[...]
